newsitem.title: INDIA: India 96/97 soybean output seen at 4.0 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: India 96/97 soybean output seen at 4.0 mln tonnes.

text.p: India's 1996/97 (November-October) soybean crop is estimated at four million tonnes compared to 4.2 million in the previous year, an official of the Soybean Processors Association of India (SOPA) said on Friday.
"The final estimate of 1996/97 soybean crop is four million tonnes," SOPA secretary general V.N. Shroff told Reuters.
SOPA had earlier anticipated 1996/97 soybean output at 4.4 million tonnes but lowered it after excessive rains in the last week of October.

"Crop harvesting and threshing operations require clear weather but unfortunately in the last week of October extensive rains in central India not only affected harvesting and threshing but damaged the crop and crop quality to a great extent," Shroff said.
SOPA estimated the area under soybean in 1996/97 at five million hectares.
Indian exporters have so far signed contracts to export nearly 710,000 tonnes of soymeal for November, December and January shipments, traders said
They said loading for November shipments were in progress in six to seven vessels at the western Indian ports.
Soymeal prices were dull due to limited export demand and quoted at $260-262 per tonne F.A.S, down from $275 per tonne on Tuesday, traders said.
Soybean was quoted at 10,200-10,500 rupees per tonne in the markets of central India, the hub of India's soybean industry.
In plant delivery conditions soybean was quoted at 10,400-10,550 rupees per tonne, against 8,800-8,900 per tonne at the same time last year, traders said.
